title: The payroll diversion
brief: 18:32. Leila asks you to clear the payroll inbox while she is in a meeting. One email asks to move a salary to a new bank account before Friday.
insight: A composite of many real cases: one convincing email to payroll, and a month's salary goes to a stranger. Every name here is fictional.
teaches: Never change bank details on the strength of an email
Verify with the employee on the number HR already holds
Report attempts so payroll can watch for the next one

message.text: Sam, could you clear the payroll inbox while I am in the budget meeting? There is a bank change in the HR portal. Usual rules!

mail.subject: Change of bank details before Friday
body: I have switched banks. Please update my salary account before Friday's payroll: Crestline Bank, sort code 40-11-09, account {{acct}}.
I am on the road all week, so email is best. Thanks!

spf.explain: Sent by a free mail service, not by Veltrix.

dkim.explain: Signed by the free mail service.

dmarc.explain: Passes for the free mail domain, which proves nothing about Jordan.

headers.summary: Jordan's real address is j.patel@veltrix-logistics.com. Anyone can open a free mail account in someone else's name.

choices.label: Did you email payroll to change your bank details?

script.say: No! I have not changed banks, and that is not my email. I have been here all week. Please do not touch my pay.

setup.title: Chat
setup.body: Leila Haddad: could you clear the payroll inbox?

outcome.label: Checked the sender's real address
outcome.what: A free mail account with Jordan's name on it, not his Veltrix address.
outcome.ideal: checks where a bank change request really came from.

outcome.label: Read the headers
outcome.what: Every check passes for the free mail domain, which proves nothing about who wrote it.
outcome.ideal: knows passing checks only prove the sending domain.

outcome.label: Read the change in the HR portal
outcome.what: Requested by email, from an outside address, with no verification.
outcome.ideal: reads where a change came from before deciding.

outcome.label: Called Jordan on the number HR holds
outcome.what: Jordan has not changed banks and has never used that address.
outcome.ideal: verifies a salary change with the employee on a number already on file.

decide.objective: Decide what to do with Jordan Patel's bank change (HR-3317).
decide.insight: Payroll diversion is quiet: nobody notices until the real employee asks where their salary went.

hint.text: Check the email's real sender. Find Jordan's desk number in the HR portal (People), call him on the desk phone (4486), then reject HR-3317 in the HR portal.

outcome.label: Approved the salary change
outcome.what: On Friday, Jordan's salary goes to the attacker's account. Jordan finds out when rent is due.
outcome.ideal: never changes bank details from an email alone.

card.title: Friday's salary, gone
body: The request came from a free mail account with Jordan's name on it. On Friday his salary will land in an account the attacker empties within the hour.
Jordan was one call away on 4486. The HR portal says it plainly: changes are made by the employee, signed in as themselves, or after a call to them.
card.ideal: verifies with the employee on a number already held, and rejects email requests.

outcome.label: Rejected the change
outcome.what: Jordan's pay goes where it always has.

card.title: Jordan gets paid
body: You rejected it. The email used Jordan's name on a free mail account, and Jordan had never heard of it.
In the real cases this is modelled on, the one control that works every time is a call to the employee on a number the company already holds.
card.ideal: verifies by phone and rejects email requests.

auto.text: Report the attempt so payroll can watch for the next one.

hint.text: Raise a Helpdesk ticket under payment or bank detail fraud.

outcome.label: Reported the diversion attempt
outcome.what: Payroll can check for similar requests about other staff.
